Description: The Asteraceae family, commonly known as the aster, daisy, or composite family, is a very large and widespread group of flowering plants with over 32,000 species.
Rosaceae is a medium-sized family of flowering plants, including about 4,828 species in 91 genera, characterized by showy flowers with five petals and numerous stamens.

Liliaceae consists of monocotyledonous, perennial, herbaceous, often bulbous geophytes with large flowers and are traditionally used extensively in decorative gardening and floral arrangements worldwide.
Orchidaceae is a diverse and widespread family of flowering plants, with blooms that are often colorful and fragrant, representing one of the two largest families of flowering plants.
Iridaceae is a family of plants in the order Asparagales, taking its name from the Iris genus, containing roughly 66 genera and totaling over 2,244 species globally.
Lamiaceae or Labiatae is a family of flowering plants commonly known as the mint or deadnettle or sage family, containing many widely used culinary and medicinal herbs.

Ranunculaceae, the buttercup or crowfoot family, is a family of over 2,000 known species of flowering plants distributed worldwide, especially in temperate and cold regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
Papaveraceae is an economically important family of about 44 genera and 770 species of flowering plants in the order Ranunculales, often known colloquially as the poppy family.
Boraginaceae is the borage or forget-me-not family, including a variety of shrubs, trees, and herbs totaling about 2,000 species in 146 genera found across the globe.
Fabaceae or Leguminosae, commonly known as the legume, pea, or bean family, is a large and economically important family of flowering plants with distinct fruit structures called legumes.
